museum: Museu Nacional (Universidade Federal do Rio de Janeiro)
other_numbers: UNKNOWN (1960 museum inventory number system; relation to Kitchen & Beltrão 1990 entries not verified)
classification_basis: description: 'única do acervo ... que apresenta um envoltório completo, disposto em camadas parcialmente conservadas'; wrapped hatchling with linen layers and vegetal-fibre padding; distal tail broken (3 tail pieces later found in box of Nº 274)
provenance: UNKNOWN; Alberto Childe's handwritten notebooks attribute 'Fayum' as probable origin of the crocodile hatchlings (per Santos & Locks 2005)
acquisition: Nicolau Fiengo collection, purchased by Emperor D. Pedro I on 3 April 1827 and given to the Museu Real (per Santos & Locks 2005)
date_period: Greco-Roman period (Período Greco-Romano, per Santos & Locks 2005 fig. caption)
description: Hatchling crocodile mummy with complex wrapping: head in two linen layers; outer layer painted black with traces of decoration; three c. 1 cm bands at neck; body padded with vegetal fibres to reconstruct the animal's shape, covered by simple linen wrapping; tail in several linen layers with black bands (max. 2 cm wide); distal portion broken.
bibliography: Santos, M. E. & Locks, M. 2005. Templos, crocodilos e múmias: ex-votos de Sobek da coleção do Museu Nacional. Revista Uniandrade (Especial História, Curitiba) 6(1): 29-48 (author reprint PDF); Kitchen, K. A. & Beltrão, M. C. 1990, Catálogo da Coleção do Egito Antigo existente no Museu Nacional, vol. 2, pp. 211, 230-232 (reproduces 1960 inventory; not seen)
source_of_identification: Scholarly description of each specimen, studied first-hand by the authors (M. Locks, Setor de Arqueologia, Museu Nacional) from 1998
notes: STATUS: object documented in the Museu Nacional in 1998-2005; the Egyptian collection was largely destroyed in the fire of 2 Sept 2018 (only c. 200 of >700 Egyptian items reported rescued by 2019); current survival of this crocodile mummy NOT verified (official page museunacional.ufrj.br could not be opened: TLS/503). Recorded PROBABLE for that reason; CONFIRMED as of 2005.

classification_basis: text only: listed as 'una cría de cocodrilo' among animal mummies acquired 1912 (González et al. 2020); no image or description; CT not yet performed
provenance: bought in the Luxor market (antigua Tebas) in 1912 (Begerock et al. 2021: 39); ancient findspot UNKNOWN
acquisition: Emilio Bacardí Moreau, trip to Egypt 1912, for the Museo Municipal of Santiago de Cuba
description: Juvenile crocodile mummy acquired with a cat, a falcon and an ibis mummy; animal mummies now in museum storage (depósitos).
bibliography: González, M., Begerock, A. M., Leonard, Y. & Faltings, D. 2020, Trabajos de Egiptología 11, p. 145; Begerock, A.-M. et al. 2021, Cuba Arqueológica 14(1): 33-46, pp. 39, 41
source_of_identification: Scholarly articles co-authored by the museum's museologist (Y. Leonard) and the Cuban Mummy Project
notes: Begerock et al. 2021 warn that animal mummies may be fakes and require CT for taxonomic classification; so identity as crocodile is not yet scientifically verified. News source OnCubaNews 2024-02-18 (candidate-only) also lists 'un cocodrilo' among the mummified animals.
